name: Second Sunrise Solar
old_description: The average home can save between $10,000 and $30,000 over the lifetime of your solar panel system.
about:
Second Sunrise Solar operates from Mt Pleasant, South Carolina, serving residential and commercial customers across the region. The company describes itself as family-run, a detail echoed in customer reviews, though no founding year or founder names are disclosed publicly. It began with a focus on guiding homeowners through the full solar adoption process, from initial consultation to long-term system monitoring.

The firm provides turnkey solar installation, handling design, permitting, financing, and grid interconnection in-house. Its service includes a Gold Star Certified Building Performance Institute (BPI) energy audit, followed by efficiency upgrades such as insulation, air and duct sealing, smart thermostats, radiant barriers, solar attic fans, LED lighting, and hybrid water heaters. All panels, racking, and inverters carry a 25-year parts and production warranty, while workmanship is covered for 10 years.

Customers include homeowners seeking to reduce utility bills and businesses facing rising commercial electricity rates. The company cites residential and commercial solar as its primary markets, with an emphasis on maximizing available tax credits and local incentives. Reviews reference projects in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic, suggesting a multi-state service area.

Second Sunrise Solar differentiates itself by managing the entire project lifecycle rather than subcontracting installation, a model it says ensures quality control and cost containment. The BPI audit-first approach aims to reduce overall energy demand before sizing the solar array, a sequence the company says improves long-term financial returns.

name: Semiconductor Support Services, Co
old_description: Our mission is to partner with our customers and enable them to sustain and improve their operations, using our high quality services and products.
about:
Semiconductor Support Services Co. (SSSco) was established in 2001 and is headquartered in Austin, Texas. The company operates offices across North America and maintains a global network of employees and partners.

SSSco delivers products and services for semiconductor wafer fabrication equipment, specializing in Applied Materials (AMAT), MKS, SMC, Lam Research, and Tokyo Electron (TEL) systems. Its offerings include the Penulator™ product family—remote, data, video, and single-board computer solutions—along with equipment upgrades, retrofits, repair services, training, and on-site support. The company maintains a large inventory of OEM and alternative qualified parts, and operates a repair center and upgrade center.

The company serves semiconductor manufacturers and equipment operators that run AMAT, MKS, SMC, Lam, and TEL wafer fab platforms. Its customers include fabs seeking productivity gains, obsolescence solutions, and sustained equipment performance through upgrades, repairs, and spare parts.

SSSco states its mission is to partner with customers to sustain and improve their operations through high-quality services and products, emphasizing rapid response with the tagline “When it has to be right…now.”

name: Seneca Foods Corporation
old_description: At Seneca, we produce seeds, harvest crops, manufacture our own containers, and provide a wide range of nutritious fruit and vegetable products.
about:
Seneca Foods Corporation is headquartered in Ripon, Wisconsin. Founded in 1949, the company began as a family-rooted enterprise and has grown into a publicly traded, vertically integrated food processor. While no individual founders are named in public records, the business emphasizes multi-generational family pride and a conservative financial approach that has guided its expansion.

Seneca manages the full spectrum of production, from seed development and crop harvesting to manufacturing its own containers and processing a wide range of fruit and vegetable products. The company operates multiple plants across the United States and sources raw materials from more than 1,400 American farms. Its portfolio includes branded lines such as Green Giant Vegetables, Aunt Nellie’s, Libby’s Vegetables, CherryMan, Read Salads, Green Valley, and Seneca Snacks, covering items like peas, cherries, and cannellini beans.

The company serves retail, foodservice, and industrial customers seeking shelf-stable and packaged produce. Its product catalog is positioned for organizational buyers, and its brands appear on grocery shelves nationwide. Seneca’s integrated model allows it to supply both private-label and national-brand accounts.

Seneca differentiates itself through complete vertical integration—controlling seed, farming, processing, and packaging—and a food safety program built on seven major quality systems. The company cites its long-term grower relationships, employee loyalty, and capital investment in state-of-the-art facilities as foundations for consistent quality and shareholder value.

name: SenseICs Corporation
old_description: SenseICs is dedicated to reimagining the status quo, designing and building next-generation integrated circuits, and delivering the best possible solutions to meet the needs of our customers.
about:
SenseICs Corporation is based in Columbus, Ohio, at 1275 Kinnear Road. The company was founded by Dr. Ramy Tantawy, who serves as CEO, and Dr. Dale Shane Smith, who serves as president; both hold PhDs from The Ohio State University and bring decades of mixed-signal integrated circuit design experience from Intel, Micron Technology, and academic research.

As a fabless semiconductor provider, SenseICs designs and delivers turnkey integrated circuits and custom microelectronic solutions. Its expertise spans readout integrated circuits (ROICs) for imaging sensors, trusted microelectronics, radio-frequency design, high-speed communication, clock and data recovery, and radiation-hardened ICs capable of withstanding over 100 Mrad total ionizing dose. The company also develops diamond particle detectors and medical imaging electronics. Prototyping and production leverage multi-project wafer runs through foundry partners such as SkyWater, GlobalFoundries, and Tower Semiconductor.

SenseICs serves defense and commercial markets. Government customers include NASA, the U.S. Navy, Air Force, and Army Research Laboratory, as well as high-energy physics collaborations at CERN and Jefferson Lab. Commercial applications target AI infrastructure, advanced medical devices, robotics, and autonomous vehicles. The firm maintains close ties with The Ohio State University’s ElectroScience Laboratory and Nanotech West Lab.

The company’s stated mission is to deliver advanced turnkey ICs that drive next-generation sensors and systems for mission-critical applications. Its STRIDE values — Staying Curious, Trust, Resilience, Innovation, Diversity, Excellence — reflect a culture built on multidisciplinary collaboration and proven technology validation.
